title: Outdoor Bass Array Shootout — 4-Deep End-Fire Line vs 3:1 CSA vs Broadside Wall
description: Compares the three canonical 4-cabinet outdoor subwoofer deployments using identical 18" touring reflex subs on open turf: a 3.45 m 4-rank End-Fire progressive delay line, a compact 3-front/1-rear Cardioid Sub Array (CSA), and a 4-wide unsteered broadside wall.
design_notes: End-Fire Progressive Delay Physics (Variant 1): Spacing 4 subs 1.15 m front-to-back and delaying each forward rank by d/c_0 = 3.35 ms aligns all 4 wavefronts constructively toward the dancefloor (+Y) across the entire 30–90 Hz band while smearing rear radiation across 4 destructively phased arrivals — achieving 15–20 dB broadband stage rejection and uniform wide horizontal coverage!

3:1 Cardioid Sub Array (CSA, Variant 2): Uses zero stage depth (0.8 m footprint) by aiming 1 inverted/delayed sub backward to cancel the 3 forward subs behind the stack. Beats the Broadside Wall by > 13 dB in DJ-booth quietness, though sacrificing ~2.2 dB forward headroom relative to End-Fire because 1 of the 4 boxes works purely as an active absorber/canceler.
Broadside Wall Beaming (Variant 3): Delivers maximum coupled mutual Z_rad loading on-axis, but floods the stage behind with omnidirectional sub-bass and narrows horizontally above 65 Hz.
